questions.a: 40 per cent

questions.q: Take the relation taught for 'Transport - Roadways' and work with: nh_length = 500, total_road_length = 80. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of share_pct.
questions.a: 625 per cent

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Transport - Roadways' refers to.
questions.a: Roadways are the most economical and convenient mode of transport for short and medium distances; India has one of the largest road networks in the world, including national highways, state highways, district roads and rural roads.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Transport - Roadways'.
questions.a: Roads provide door-to-door service and flexibility, making them the most vital link for freight and passenger movement, especially where railways cannot reach.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Transport - Roadways' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Transport

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Transport - Railways' refers to.
questions.a: Railways are the principal mode of transport for heavy goods and large numbers of passengers over long distances; the Indian Railways is the largest public sector undertaking in the country.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Transport - Railways'.
questions.a: Railways bind the economic life of the country by moving bulky raw materials and goods over long distances cheaply, and by accelerating the development of agriculture and industry.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Transport - Railways' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Transport

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Transport - Pipelines' refers to.
questions.a: Pipelines are used to transport crude oil, petroleum products and natural gas from oil fields to refineries and to consumption centres; they rule out delays and losses during transit.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Transport - Pipelines'.
questions.a: Pipeline transport provides a continuous, reliable and low-loss mode for liquids and gases over long distances, connecting oil fields, refineries and cities.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Transport - Pipelines' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Transport

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Transport - Waterways' refers to.
questions.a: Waterways are the cheapest mode of transport for heavy and bulky goods over long distances; India has inland waterways on rivers and national waterways, and oceanic routes along the coast.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Transport - Waterways'.
questions.a: Water transport is the most economical for heavy and bulky goods because it requires low fuel and maintenance, but it is slow and limited by the navigability of rivers.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Transport - Waterways' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Transport

questions.q: Using the method 'Transport - Airways', work with: air_cost = 12000, rail_cost = 50000. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of cost_ratio.
questions.a: 0.24 times

questions.q: Take the relation taught for 'Transport - Airways' and work with: air_cost = 80000, rail_cost = 5000. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of cost_ratio.
questions.a: 16 times

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Transport - Airways' refers to.
questions.a: Airways are the fastest and most comfortable mode of transport, essential for remote, hilly and inaccessible areas; they are useful during natural disasters but are costly and carry limited cargo.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Transport - Airways'.
questions.a: Air transport is the fastest mode and reaches remote and difficult terrain where other modes cannot, but its high cost limits it to passengers, perishable goods and emergencies.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Transport - Airways' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Transport

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Communication - Personal and Mass' refers to.
questions.a: Communication includes personal communication (postcards, letters, telephones, internet) and mass communication (radio, television, newspapers, films) which transmit messages, news and entertainment across the country.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Communication - Personal and Mass'.
questions.a: The Indian postal network is the largest in the world, and mass communication through radio, television and print media connects people, spreads information and supports education and national integration.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Communication - Personal and Mass' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Communication

questions.a: 1140 units

questions.a: 497 units

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'International Trade' refers to.
questions.a: International trade is the exchange of goods and services between countries; exports are goods sold abroad and imports are goods bought from abroad, and the balance of trade is the difference between their values.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'International Trade'.
questions.a: A favourable balance of trade occurs when exports exceed imports; trade connects producers and consumers across nations and is essential for economic growth.

questions.q: Under which section is 'International Trade' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: International Trade

questions.q: Using the method 'Tourism as Trade', work with: avg_spending = 30, tourist_count = 75. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of earnings.
questions.a: 2250 units

questions.q: Take the relation taught for 'Tourism as Trade' and work with: avg_spending = 3, tourist_count = 200. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of earnings.
questions.a: 600 units

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Tourism as Trade' refers to.
questions.a: Tourism is an important trade that earns foreign exchange, generates employment and promotes local crafts and culture; foreign tourists bring foreign currency that boosts the economy of the host region.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Tourism as Trade'.
questions.a: Tourism contributes to foreign exchange earnings and employment; the money spent by foreign tourists is counted as an invisible export and supports handicrafts, transport and hospitality.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Tourism as Trade' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Tourism as a Trade

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Trade and Globalisation' refers to.
questions.a: Globalisation is the integration of national economies with the world economy through trade, investment and technology; it has expanded markets, increased competition and connected producers and consumers across the globe.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Trade and Globalisation'.
questions.a: Globalisation links local producers to world markets, increases the flow of goods, services and capital, and raises competition and quality, but it can also challenge small producers.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Trade and Globalisation' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Trade and Globalisation

concepts.title: Role of Transport, Communication and Logistics

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Role of Transport, Communication and Logistics' refers to.
questions.a: Transport, communication and trade together form the lifelines of the national economy; transport moves goods and people, communication transmits information, and logistics combines storage and transport to deliver goods efficiently.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Role of Transport, Communication and Logistics'.
questions.a: Efficient transport, communication and trade connect producers to markets, integrate the economy and promote national development; logistics ensures goods reach the right place at the right time.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Role of Transport, Communication and Logistics' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Transport, Communication and Trade
